name: mapiter
algorithm: Fill each language's std hash map once with 2^20 splitmix64 u64 keys (value the insertion index), then iterate it passes times adding key * (value + 1) and the length, wrapping and so order-free (README.md).

skip.c: no std hash map in C
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; iterating has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own table layout and order; the sum over every entry is order-free and checks every result
notes: Hashes and DoS posture (B20): mk Map.New, DD-5's fixed fast hash, public key; mk-keyed Map.NewKeyed, SipHash-1-3 under a random per-process key (HashKey.New); Rust HashMap, SipHash-1-3 under RandomState's random key; Zig AutoHashMap over std.heap.smp_allocator, wyhash-based autoHash with seed 0, fixed; Go map (swiss table), AES-based runtime hash seeded per map, randomised iteration start; C# Dictionary<ulong, ulong>, default ulong.GetHashCode() (fixed/unkeyed), dense entry-array iteration. Iteration does not hash; the one fill (2^20 inserts) is inside the time, and its share is not measured.
